narration.en: A phone book with a lakh names: linear search might need a lakh comparisons, binary search only seventeen. But binary search needs the names sorted. Today we weigh the two.
narration.kn: ಒಂದು ಲಕ್ಷ ಹೆಸರುಗಳ ದೂರವಾಣಿ ಪುಸ್ತಕ: ರೇಖೀಯ ಹುಡುಕಾಟಕ್ಕೆ ಲಕ್ಷ ಹೋಲಿಕೆಗಳು ಬೇಕಾಗಬಹುದು, ಬೈನರಿಗೆ ಕೇವಲ ಹದಿನೇಳು. ಆದರೆ ಬೈನರಿಗೆ ಹೆಸರುಗಳು ವಿಂಗಡಿತವಾಗಿರಬೇಕು.

body.en: The efficiency of a search is judged by the number of comparisons it needs. For n elements, linear search needs up to n comparisons, so the work grows in direct proportion to n. Binary search halves the list at each step, so it needs at most ⌊log₂ n⌋ + 1 comparisons: about 7 for 100 elements, 10 for 1,000 and 20 for a million. Doubling n adds only one step to binary search but doubles the worst case of linear search.

points.en: Doubling n: linear doubles, binary adds one

tryThis.kn: ದ್ವಿಮಾನ ವೇಗ; ಆದರೂ ರೇಖೀಯ ಏಕೆ ಬಳಸುತ್ತೇವೆ?

body.en: Linear search is simple, needs no sorting and suits small lists, unsorted data or a list searched only once. Binary search is far faster on large lists, but the list must be sorted and kept sorted when elements are added, which has its own cost. Binary search is used wherever large sorted data is searched often: dictionaries, telephone directories, sorted database indexes and roll-number lists.

points.en: Keeping data sorted has a cost
